chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from one who narrated it from Abu Basir, who said:
"When you set out after the rising of the dawn (Fajr) and you did not intend travel during the night, then complete your fast and consider it from the month of Ramadan."
ai.seo_question: Does a fast remain valid if one starts traveling after Fajr without prior intention?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the specific condition of 'intention' (niyyah) in determining travel status for fasting; since the traveler did not intend to leave before dawn, their home-city fast remains valid. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the pre-dawn intention as the decisive factor for distinguishing between the obligations of a resident and a traveler, ensuring the fast is counted as Qada or Ramadan depending on the context. It provides practical clarity for those who make spontaneous travel decisions after Fajr, preventing unnecessary invalidation of their worship.
